## Part 0: Settings and preparatory data management on open dataset

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r working directory}
rm(list=ls())
graphics.off()
setwd("~/Desktop/file_r/")
```

```{r Installed packages, include = FALSE}
install.packages(c("stm", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "tidytext", "tidyr", "tidyverse", "data.table", "haven", "readxl", "quanteda", "text2map", "quanteda.textplots", "quanteda.textstats", "text2vec", "fpc", "factoextra", "textmineR"))
```

```{r Load packages, include=FALSE}
library(stm)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidytext)
library(tidyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(data.table)
library(haven)
library(readxl)
library(quanteda) 
library(quanteda.textplots) 
library(quanteda.textstats) 
library(text2map)
library(text2vec)
library(fpc) 
library(factoextra) 
library(textmineR) 
```

```{r open data files, include=FALSE}
## [1] metadata dataset 
data <- read_xlsx("~/Desktop/file_r/data/df_complete_3.xlsx") ## Last Version from Tomasi, without merged words (Note: negative emotions such as "disappointment" and "sadness" should be higher than "neutral")
head(data) # dataset is already skimmed, only rows from final text dataset
```

```{r Preparatory recodes from VulnYouth's data management - Socio-demographic characteristics}
## Gender; it does not need any recode 
data  |> 
  count(gender)

## Age class (below vs above 30)
data |> 
  count(ageyear)

data <- data |> 
  mutate(age_dum = ifelse(ageyear >= 30, 1, 0))

data |> 
  count(age_dum)

## migrant background
data |> 
  count(migrant)

data <- data |> 
  mutate(migr_dum = ifelse(migrant == 3, 1, 0))

data |> 
  count(migr_dum)
```

```{r Preparatory recodes from VulnYouth's data management - Precarity-related indicators}
## Scale of subjectively perceived precarity - dummy
data |> 
  count(prec)

data <- data |> 
  mutate(dum_prec = ifelse(prec >= 8, 1, 0)
         )
data |> 
  count(dum_prec)

## Scale of subjectively perceived precarity - normalised index
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    normprec = (prec - min(prec, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                (max(prec, na.rm = TRUE) - min(prec, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

data |> 
  count(normprec)

## Employment VUlnerability - From Epres' Scale (higher vs lower risk) like in precarity' scale sintax
data |> 
  count(normepres) 
  
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    dum_normepres = if_else(normepres > 0.8, 1, 0))

data |> 
  count(dum_normepres)

## Job Insecurity (higher gravity vs all)
data |> 
  count(jobinsec)

data <- data |> 
  mutate(dum_jobinsec = if_else(jobinsec %in% c(1, 2), 1, 0))

data |> 
  count(dum_jobinsec)

## Making ends meet (higher difficulty vs all) 
data |> 
  count(endmeet)

data <- data |> 
  mutate(dum_endmeet = if_else(endmeet %in% c(1, 2), 1, 0))

data |> 
  count(dum_endmeet)

## Capacity to pay unexpected expenses ("alone" vs all)
data |> 
  count(unexpmix)

data <- data |> 
  mutate(dum_unexpmix = if_else(unexpmix %in% c(1), 1, 0))

data |> 
  count(dum_unexpmix)

## Economic indipendence, it does not need any dummy recode
data |> 
  count(ecoind)
```

# Quantitative Analysis

## Part 1: VAD Scores

```{r VAD scores: Valence}
## Valence - continous variable
data |>
  count(V_predicted) |>
  mutate(
    perc = 100 * (n / sum(n))           
  )

## Valence continuos - density plot and boxplot
summary(data$V_predicted)

data |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = V_predicted)) +
  geom_density() +
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept = 3)) +
  labs(
    x = "Predicted Valence Scores",
    title = "Predicted Valence - Density Plot"
  )
ggsave("Emo_Results/Valence_densityplot.png", width  = 6, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300)

## Valence - dummy variable
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    V_dum = if_else(V_predicted > 3, 1, 0)
  )

data |> 
  count(V_dum) |> 
  mutate(
    perc = 100 * (n/sum(n))
  )

## Valence_dum - bar plot
data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = V_dum)) +
  geom_bar(aes(fill = factor(V_dum))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("0" = "#1b9e77", "1" = "#d95f02"),
    labels = c("Negative", "Positive"),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Valence_dummy - bar plot",
    x = "Predicted Valence (dummy recode)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("Emo_Results/Valencedum_barplot.png", width  = 6, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

### 1.1 Descriptives VAD Scores: Valence, Arousal, Dominance [ Look at Tomasi analyses - file python ]

```{r VAD scores across socio-demographic characteristics and perceived precarity levels}
vad_by_socio_group <- data |>
  group_by(gender, age_dum, migr_dum, dum_prec) |>
  mutate(
    age_dum   = factor(age_dum,   levels = c(0,1), labels = c("< 30", ">= 30")),
    migr_dum  = factor(migr_dum,  levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No migr.", "Migr.")),
    dum_prec  = factor(dum_prec,  levels = c(0,1), labels = c("Low prec.", "High prec.")),
    gender    = factor(gender,   levels = c(0,1), labels = c("Men", "Women"))
  ) |> 
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    val_mean = mean(V_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    val_sd   = sd(V_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    aro_mean = mean(A_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    aro_sd   = sd(A_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    dom_mean = mean(D_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    dom_sd   = sd(D_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )
tibble(vad_by_socio_group)
```

```{r chi-results VAD dimensions and listed variables}
library(broom)
socio_cat_vars <- c("gender", "age_dum", "migr_dum", "dum_prec")

## Valence
V_socio_chi_results <- map_dfr(
  socio_cat_vars,
  ~ chisq.test(data[[.x]], data$V_dum) |>
    tidy() |>
    mutate(var = .x),
  .id = NULL
)
tibble(V_socio_chi_results) # Only gender has passed the p-value test

## Arousal
A_socio_chi_results <- map_dfr(
  socio_cat_vars,
  ~ chisq.test(data[[.x]], data$A_dum) |>
    tidy() |>
    mutate(var = .x),
  .id = NULL
)
tibble(A_socio_chi_results) # Only gender has passed the p-value test

## Dominance
D_socio_chi_results <- map_dfr(
  socio_cat_vars,
  ~ chisq.test(data[[.x]], data$D_dum) |>
    tidy() |>
    mutate(var = .x),
  .id = NULL
)
tibble(D_socio_chi_results) # Only gender has passed the p-value test
```

```{r control of attended frequencies - Valence}
## Gender x V
tab_gender_V <- table(data$gender, data$V_dum)
chi_gender_V <- chisq.test(tab_gender_V, correct = FALSE) |> print() # only gender has passed the significance test with X-squared = 4.0144, p-value = 0.04511
## Expected and observed
chi_gender_V$expected   
chi_gender_V$observed 

## age_dum x V
tab_age_V <- table(data$age_dum, data$V_dum)
chi_age_V <- chisq.test(tab_age_V, correct = FALSE) |> print()
chi_age_V$expected
chi_age_V$observed

## migr_dum × V
tab_migr_V <- table(data$migr_dum, data$V_dum)
chi_migr_V <- chisq.test(tab_migr_V, correct = FALSE) |> print()
chi_migr_V$expected
chi_migr_V$observed

## dum_prec × V
tab_prec_V <- table(data$dum_prec, data$V_dum)
chi_prec_V <- chisq.test(tab_prec_V, correct = FALSE) |> print()
chi_prec_V$expected
chi_prec_V$observed

## Each pair has passed the attended frequencies test (at least >= 5 observation for each cell) meaning that chisq is correct to perform the test chisq to measure association between variables (i.e. Valence and x sociodemographic characteristics)
```

```{r control of attended frequencies - Arousal}
## gender × A
tab_gender_A <- table(data$gender, data$A_dum)
chi_gender_A <- chisq.test(tab_gender_A, correct = FALSE) |> print() # p-value = 0.05935 X-squared = 3.5555, as above
chi_gender_A$expected
chi_gender_A$observed

## age_dum × A
tab_age_A <- table(data$age_dum, data$A_dum)
chi_age_A <- chisq.test(tab_age_A, correct = FALSE) |> print()
chi_age_A$expected
chi_age_A$observed

## migr_dum × A
tab_migr_A <- table(data$migr_dum, data$A_dum)
chi_migr_A <- chisq.test(tab_migr_A, correct = FALSE) |> print()
chi_migr_A$expected
chi_migr_A$observed

## dum_prec × A
tab_prec_A <- table(data$dum_prec, data$A_dum)
chi_prec_A <- chisq.test(tab_prec_A, correct = FALSE) |> print() # p-value = 0.07231 almost accetable(?)
chi_prec_A$expected
chi_prec_A$observed

## As above, test of attendend frequencies passed
```

```{r control of attended frequencies - Dominance}
## gender × D
tab_gender_D <- table(data$gender, data$D_dum)
chi_gender_D <- chisq.test(tab_gender_D, correct = FALSE) |> print() # X-squared = 6.5191, df = 1, p-value = 0.01067 highly significative 
chi_gender_D$expected
chi_gender_D$observed

## age_dum × D
tab_age_D <- table(data$age_dum, data$D_dum)
chi_age_D <- chisq.test(tab_age_D, correct = FALSE) |> print()
chi_age_D$expected
chi_age_D$observed

## migr_dum × D
tab_migr_D <- table(data$migr_dum, data$D_dum)
chi_migr_D <- chisq.test(tab_migr_D, correct = FALSE) |> print()
chi_migr_D$expected
chi_migr_D$observed

## dum_prec × D
tab_prec_D <- table(data$dum_prec, data$D_dum)
chi_prec_D <- chisq.test(tab_prec_D, correct = FALSE) |> print()
chi_prec_D$expected
chi_prec_D$observed

## As above, test of attendend frequencies passed
```

### 1.2 Descriptives and association levels VAD Scores per socio-demographic characteristics and perceived precarity levels

```{r Valence across socio-demographic and precarity groups}
data |>
  mutate(
    age_dum   = factor(age_dum,   levels = c(0,1), labels = c("< 30", ">= 30")),
    migr_dum  = factor(migr_dum,  levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No migr.", "Migr.")),
    dum_prec  = factor(dum_prec,  levels = c(0,1), labels = c("Low prec.", "High prec.")),
    gender    = factor(gender,   levels = c(0,1), labels = c("Men", "Women"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dum_prec, y = V_predicted, fill = gender)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.alpha = 0.4, position = position_dodge(width = 0.75)) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = "mean",
    geom = "point",
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
    shape = 21, size = 2, color = "black"
  ) +
  facet_grid(migr_dum ~ age_dum) +
  labs(
    x = "Subjective precarity",
    y = "Valence score",
    fill = "Gender",
    title = "Valence across socio-demographic and precarity groups"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10)
ggsave("Emo_Results/Valence across socio-demographic and precarity groups.png", width  = 6, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

### 1.3 Boxplot descriptives VAD dimensions across socio-demographic and precarity groups

```{r VAD Scores per drivers of multidimensional precarity}
vad_by_prec_group <- data |>
  group_by(dum_normepres, dum_jobinsec, dum_endmeet, dum_unexpmix, ecoind) |>
  mutate(
    dum_normepres   = factor(dum_normepres,   levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    dum_jobinsec  = factor(dum_jobinsec,  levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    dum_endmeet  = factor(dum_endmeet,  levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    dum_unexpmix = factor(dum_unexpmix,   levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    ecoind = factor(ecoind,   levels = c(0,1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
  ) |> 
  summarise(
    n        = n(),
    val_mean = mean(V_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    val_sd   = sd(V_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    aro_mean = mean(A_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    aro_sd   = sd(A_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    dom_mean = mean(D_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    dom_sd   = sd(D_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )
tibble(vad_by_prec_group)
```

```{r VAD scores per drivers of multidimensional precarity}
prec_cat_vars <- c("dum_normepres", "dum_jobinsec", "dum_endmeet", "dum_unexpmix", "ecoind")

## Valence
V_prec_chi_results <- map_dfr(
  prec_cat_vars,
  ~ chisq.test(data[[.x]], data$V_dum) |>
    tidy() |>
    mutate(var = .x),
  .id = NULL
)
tibble(V_prec_chi_results) # No significance (p-value)

## Arousal
A_prec_chi_results <- map_dfr(
  prec_cat_vars,
  ~ chisq.test(data[[.x]], data$A_dum) |>
    tidy() |>
    mutate(var = .x),
  .id = NULL
)
tibble(A_prec_chi_results) # (p-value) significance for unexpected expensens and economic indipendence, almost acceptable vulnerability in employment (0.08691230)

## Dominance
D_prec_chi_results <- map_dfr(
  prec_cat_vars,
  ~ chisq.test(data[[.x]], data$D_dum) |>
    tidy() |>
    mutate(var = .x),
  .id = NULL
)
tibble(D_prec_chi_results) # (p-value) significance making ends meet 
```

### 1.6 Boxplot Descriptives Arousal by precarity drivers

```{r Dominance by precarity drivers - boxplots}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# --- 1. Data Preparation ---
# Ensure factors are labeled correctly for the plot
data_plot <- data |>
  mutate(
    # Recode Precarity Group (0/1 to Low/High)
    dum_prec_label = factor(dum_prec, 
                            levels = c(0, 1), 
                            labels = c("Low Prec.", "High Prec.")),
    # Recode Gender (0/1 to Men/Women - adjust based on your specific coding)
    gender_label = factor(gender, 
                          levels = c(0, 1), 
                          labels = c("Men", "Women"))
  )

# --- 2. Create the Left Plot: Valence ---
p_valence <- data_plot |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dum_prec_label, y = V_predicted, fill = gender_label)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.alpha = 0.4, outlier.size = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#f8766d", "#00bfc4")) + # Salmon/Teal colors
  labs(
    x = "Subjective Precarity",
    y = "Valence Score (1-5)",
    title = "A. Valence"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none") # Hide legend for the first plot to save space

# --- 3. Create the Right Plot: Dominance ---
p_dominance <- data_plot |>
  ggplot(aes(x = dum_prec_label, y = D_predicted, fill = gender_label)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.alpha = 0.4, outlier.size = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#f8766d", "#00bfc4")) +
  labs(
    x = "Subjective Precarity",
    y = "Dominance Score (1-5)",
    title = "B. Dominance",
    fill = "Gender"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11)

# --- 4. Combine and Save ---
# Use patchwork to place them side-by-side
combined_plot <- p_valence + p_dominance

print(combined_plot)

# Save with dimensions that fit a standard thesis page width
ggsave("Emo_Results/Valence_Dominance_SideBySide.png", combined_plot, width = 9, height = 4.5, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

### 1.7 Boxplot descriptives Dominance by precarity drivers

```{r VAD scores per normalised self-perceived precarity - normalisation and correlation test}
## To keep same measurement scale we normalised VAD score

## Valence - normalised
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    V_norm = (V_predicted - min(V_predicted, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                (max(V_predicted, na.rm = TRUE) - min(V_predicted, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

data |> 
  count(V_norm)

## Arousal - normalised 
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    A_norm = (A_predicted - min(A_predicted, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                (max(A_predicted, na.rm = TRUE) - min(A_predicted, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

data |> 
  count(A_norm)

## Dominance - normalised 
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    D_norm = (D_predicted - min(D_predicted, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                (max(D_predicted, na.rm = TRUE) - min(D_predicted, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

data |> 
  count(D_norm)

## Calcuted correlation and p-value
## All variables are significative, but with weakly correlation
cor.test(data$normprec, data$V_norm) # 0.07954171 
cor.test(data$normprec, data$A_norm) # 0.04536515
cor.test(data$normprec, data$D_norm) # 0.0521304
```

### 1.5 Scatterplots normalised VAD Scores per normalised self-perceived precarity

```{r stepwise regression model - normalised precarity as a function of vad scores (normalised)}
## model may pass p-value test but with low adjusted R2 (i.e. explained variability of outcome variable)

## Valence
model_val <- lm(normprec ~ V_norm, data = data)
summary(model_val)

## Arousal
model_aro <- lm(normprec ~ A_norm, data = data)
summary(model_aro)

## Dominance
model_dom <- lm(normprec ~ D_norm, data = data)
summary(model_dom)

## VAD Model
model_vad <- lm(normprec ~ V_norm + A_norm + D_norm, data = data)
summary(model_vad) # all independents variables are significatives, however polarity of valence should be switched - from positive to negative - to be meaningful
```

```{r stepwise regression model - normalised precarity as a function of vad scores (predicted)}
## Looking at adjusted R-squared (e.g. 0.01251 in the first model),  unfortunately it's very low explained variance in the outcome variable 

## VAD predicted
model_vadpredicted <- lm(normprec ~ V_predicted + A_predicted + D_predicted, data = data)
summary(model_vadpredicted) # same as above with Predicted values (-3,+3)

## Valence predicted
model_valpredicted <- lm(normprec ~ V_predicted, data = data)
summary(model_valpredicted) # positive (why? because it starts from zero?) higly significative 

## Arousal predicted
model_aropredicted <- lm(normprec ~ A_predicted, data = data)
summary(model_aropredicted) # positive, midly significative

## Dominance predicted
model_dompredicted <- lm(normprec ~ D_predicted, data = data)
summary(model_dompredicted) # effect is positive (why?) not very significative
```

### 1.9 Regression Models: (Normprec) function of VAD (Normalised and Predicted scores)

```{r stepwise regression model - sociodemographic characteristics}
## Model changed from linear to logit 

model_logit <- glm(dum_prec ~ factor(V_dum) + factor(A_dum) + factor(D_dum), data = data, family = binomial)
summary(model_logit) # arousal weakly significative

model_socio1 <- glm(dum_prec ~ factor(V_dum) + factor(A_dum) + factor(D_dum) + factor(gender), data = data, family = binomial)
summary(model_socio1) # only gender and arousal are respectively midly and weakly significative

model_socio2 <- glm(dum_prec ~ factor(V_dum) + factor(A_dum) + factor(D_dum) + factor(gender) + factor(age_dum), data = data, family = binomial)
summary(model_socio2)

model_socio3 <- glm(dum_prec ~ factor(V_dum) + factor(A_dum) + factor(D_dum) + factor(gender) + factor(age_dum) + factor(migr_dum), data = data, family = binomial)
summary(model_socio3)
```

### 1.10 Sociodemographic Regression Models

```{r stepwise regression model - precarity related indicators}
## As expected all previously tested indicators are reliable and distinctive indicators of precarity. VAD dimensions are not meaningful when precarity-related indicators are included in the model 

model_prec1 <- glm(dum_prec ~ factor(V_dum) + factor(A_dum) + factor(D_dum) + factor(dum_normepres), data = data, family = binomial)
summary(model_prec1)

model_prec2 <- glm(dum_prec ~ factor(V_dum) + factor(A_dum) + factor(D_dum) + factor(dum_normepres) + factor(dum_jobinsec), data = data, family = binomial)
summary(model_prec2)

model_prec3 <- glm(dum_prec ~ factor(V_dum) + factor(A_dum) + factor(D_dum) + factor(dum_normepres) + factor(dum_jobinsec) + factor(dum_endmeet), data = data, family = binomial)
summary(model_prec3)

model_prec4 <- glm(dum_prec ~ factor(V_dum) + factor(A_dum) + factor(D_dum) + factor(dum_normepres) + factor(dum_jobinsec) + factor(dum_endmeet) + factor(dum_unexpmix), data = data, family = binomial)
summary(model_prec4)

model_prec5 <- glm(dum_prec ~ factor(V_dum) + factor(A_dum) + factor(D_dum) + factor(dum_normepres) + factor(dum_jobinsec) + factor(dum_endmeet) + factor(dum_unexpmix) + factor(ecoind), data = data, family = binomial)
summary(model_prec5)
```

```{r Subsetting dataset}
## Subset the original dataset
emo_data <- data |> 
  select(ID, gender, age_dum, migr_dum, dum_prec, normprec, dum_normepres,dum_jobinsec, dum_endmeet, dum_unexpmix, ecoind, V_predicted, A_predicted, D_predicted, V_dum, A_dum, D_dum, ends_with("_pred"))
```

```{r Transform subset from wide to long}
## Only emotions are transformed
emo_data <- emo_data |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = ends_with("_pred"),
    names_to = "emotion",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    emotion = str_remove(emotion, "_pred$")
  )
glimpse(emo_data)
```

### 2.0 Subsetting of original dataset and transformation from wide-to-long

```{r Barplot predicted emotions - with neutral included}
emo_data |>

  summarise(

  ggplot(aes(x = emotion, y = perc)) +
```

### 2.3 Predicted emotion per socio-demographic characteristics (logistic regression models - ungrouped emotions)

Negative emotions such as disappointment and sadness are far more likely than other emotions in both genders, and although small percentage differences emerge between men and women, the logistic model does not detect significant gender effects on the probabilities of the predicted emotions, so the overall emotional pattern is largely overlapping across groups. In the materials analysed, precarity is thematized as a strongly negative condition in a broadly shared way: the discrete emotions that surface (especially disappointment and sadness) characterize all groups similarly, and the models show no significant interaction effects between precariousness or gender and specific emotions, suggesting that precariousness, as defined and narrated by the respondents, operates primarily as a common stressor rather than as an emotionally differentiated experience across social groups.

```{r Predicted Emotions per drivers of precarity - economic independence}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Identify the Top 5 Emotions generally

  count(emotion, wt = value) |>

  )

# 3. Create the Grouped Bar Plot

# Calculate Correlation

# Plot Heatmap

 theme_minimal() + 
 theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1,
```

## Part 3: Sentiment Groups - Grouped Predicted Emotions -

```{r Sentiment groups recode}
# I will use the original wide dataset (data non emo_data)
data <- data |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    any_pos = any(c_across(c(admiration_pred, amusement_pred, approval_pred,
                             caring_pred, curiosity_pred, desire_pred,
                             excitement_pred, gratitude_pred, joy_pred,
                             love_pred, optimism_pred, pride_pred,
                             realization_pred, relief_pred, surprise_pred)) == 1),
    any_neg = any(c_across(c(anger_pred, annoyance_pred, confusion_pred,
                             disappointment_pred, disapproval_pred, disgust_pred,
                             embarrassment_pred, fear_pred, grief_pred,
                             nervousness_pred, remorse_pred, sadness_pred)) == 1),
    only_neu = (neutral_pred == 1 & !any_pos & !any_neg),
    sentiment_group = case_when(
      only_neu           ~ "Neutral",
      any_pos & !any_neg ~ "Positive",
      any_neg & !any_pos ~ "Negative",
      any_pos & any_neg  ~ "Ambivalent",
      TRUE               ~ "Neutral"
    ),
    sentiment_group = factor(
      sentiment_group,
      levels = c("Neutral","Positive", "Negative", "Ambivalent")
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

data |> 
  count(sentiment_group) # I confirm frequencies on Tomasi's python sintax 

# bar plot sentiment_group
data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sentiment_group)) +
  geom_bar(aes(fill = factor(sentiment_group))) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("1" = "#B0B0B0",  "2" = "#1B9E77",  "3" = "#D95F02",  "4" = "#7570B3"),
    labels = c("Neutral","Positive", "Negative", "Ambivalent"),
    name   = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Predicted Sentiment Groups - bar plot",
    x = "Predicted emotions (sentiment groups recode)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("Emo_Results/Predicted Sentiment Groups - bar plot.png", width  = 6, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

```{r TextPreprocessing}
# See in STM_DiLiberatore_Model (Script) the key factor to replicate Di Liberatore's 20k model was the stoplist
## Load Di liberatore Environment
#load("C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_Emotion/Emo_Processed Data/environment_diLiberatore.RData")

## load the last version of my dataset
data_last <- readRDS("~/Desktop/file_r/data/dataset_last.rds")

emo_processed <- textProcessor(
  documents = data_last$text,
  metadata = data_last,
  language = "english",
  stem = TRUE,
  removestopwords = TRUE,       
  customstopwords = words, # this is the final stoplist
  custompunctuation = c("-"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

emo_out <- prepDocuments(
  documents = emo_processed$documents,
  vocab = emo_processed$vocab,
  meta = emo_processed$meta
)

emo_docs <- emo_out$documents
emo_vocab <- emo_out$vocab
emo_meta <- emo_out$meta

# Removing 720 of 1581 terms (720 of 16532 tokens) due to frequency 
# Removing 14 Documents with No Words 
# Your corpus now has 2459 documents, 861 terms and 15812 tokens.
```

```{r base model - Di Liberatore 2025}
               vocab = emo_vocab,
```

```{r top2 relevant Documents per topics - Ungrouped Predicted Emotions}
## Ungrouped predicted emotions

# open a loop
K <- m_ungrp_predemo$settings$dim$K  # total number of topics in the STM
# save results in pdf
pdf("C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_Emotion/Emo_Results/STM_Topic_Quotes_Model_with_ungrouped_emotions.pdf", width = 8, height = 6)

for (k in 1:K) {
  # findThoughts returns a list $docs, where each element corresponds to one topic
  # Here we extract the first (and only) element for the current topic k
  thoughts_ungrp <- findThoughts(m_ungrp_predemo,
                           texts = ans_lis_filter,
                           n = 2,      # number of representative phrases per topic
                           topics = k)$docs[[1]]
  
  # Plot the representative phrases for the current topic
  plotQuote(thoughts_ungrp,
            main = paste("Topic", k),
            width = 80,     # maximum line width for each phrase
            text.cex = 0.8) # font size for the text
}
#close pdf
dev.off()
```

```{r Estimate effects}
K <- model_base$settings$dim$K 
for (k in 1:K) {
effects_emopred_ungrp <- estimateEffect(1:K ~ admiration_pred + amusement_pred + anger_pred + annoyance_pred + approval_pred + caring_pred + confusion_pred + curiosity_pred + desire_pred + disappointment_pred + disapproval_pred + disgust_pred + embarrassment_pred + excitement_pred + fear_pred + gratitude_pred + grief_pred + joy_pred + love_pred + nervousness_pred + optimism_pred + pride_pred + neutral_pred,  
                          stmobj = m_ungrp_predemo,
                          metadata = emo_meta, 
                          uncertainty = "Global")

effects_emopred_grp <- estimateEffect(1:K ~ sentiment_group,  
                          stmobj = m_grp_predemo,
                          metadata = emo_meta, 
                          uncertainty = "Global")
}

saveRDS(effects_emopred_ungrp, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_Emotion/Emo_Processed Data/Effect_predicted_ungrouped.rds")
saveRDS(effects_emopred_grp, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_Emotion/Emo_Processed Data/Effect_predicted_grouped.rds")
```
